inspectedCallSites.role: Loads one stage-selected stable-environment authority envelope.
inspectedCallSites.resultAndErrorBoundary: Returns the branded authority path and maps every metadata, JSON, envelope, or stage-policy failure to stable-environment-authority-invalid.

inspectedCallSites.role: Validates the Preview configuration authority before decoding the remaining configuration input.
inspectedCallSites.resultAndErrorBoundary: Returns the branded authority path and maps the authority boundary to preview-configuration-authority-invalid.

inspectedCallSites.role: Validates read-only inventory authority before provider reads and separately validates and writes inventory and receipt artifacts.
inspectedCallSites.pathPolicy: Repository-relative, bounded to 240 characters, with pairwise authority/artifact/receipt path exclusion.
inspectedCallSites.resultAndErrorBoundary: Returns the authority path from validation, then returns encoded receipt JSON after two distinct mode-0600 writes.

inspectedCallSites.role: Reads authority and manifest inputs for stage-selected state plan, apply, or restore operations and writes a bounded receipt.
inspectedCallSites.pathPolicy: Repository-relative, bounded to 240 characters, with four-way authority/manifest/backup/receipt path exclusion.
inspectedCallSites.resultAndErrorBoundary: Returns the stage migration result, preserves structured observed/expected counts, and maps capability failures through StateMigrationFailure.

inspectedCallSites.role: Reads authority and manifest inputs, proves remote-state and credential-leak invariants, and writes one bounded receipt.
inspectedCallSites.pathPolicy: Repository-relative, bounded to 240 characters, with three-way authority/manifest/receipt path exclusion.
inspectedCallSites.resultAndErrorBoundary: Returns a binding-profile-specific proof result and deliberately translates configuration, authority, manifest, state, credential, and receipt failures separately.

inspectedCallSites.role: Validates Preview report-only authority and binds the report to the exact authority artifact bytes.
inspectedCallSites.resultAndErrorBoundary: Returns a SHA-256 fingerprint of the raw authority bytes, then writes different report and receipt result shapes.

inspectedCallSites.role: Validates one project-global Vercel Git-link authority envelope.
inspectedCallSites.resultAndErrorBoundary: Emits only a bounded valid-status JSON object and collapses authority-boundary failures to vercel-git-link-authority-invalid.

genuinelyCommonPolicy: Authority paths are Schema-decoded before file access.
Authority inputs require mode 0600, a bounded size, JSON decoding, the shared authority-envelope schema, and one capability-owned task policy.
Ajv validation is strict-false and accumulates errors without exposing raw authority or validation detail.
Secret values and raw provider data do not enter receipts or failure output.
deliberatelyVariablePolicy: Authority-only readers use a 64 KiB ceiling while state migration and adoption proof use a 2 MiB fixed-contract input ceiling because the same reader also admits manifests.
The drift reader must hash the raw authority bytes before they are discarded; other readers return a branded path or no authority-derived value.
Some Ajv instances disable format validation and others retain the default; the owning task schemas and historical fixtures determine that choice.
Stage-selected policy schemas, path-conflict sets, receipt schemas, artifact counts, return shapes, and safe failure vocabularies differ by capability.

The seven infrastructure authority inputs are repository-relative, while the adjacent Photon webhook boundary deliberately requires an absolute output path; a cross-package API would have to admit both policies.
State migration preserves structured tagged-error counts, adoption proof translates granular string reasons, and the remaining readers expose different bounded results.
sharedApiSurfaceRisk: A common reader would need callbacks or strategy parameters for raw-byte fingerprinting, stage-policy selection, task Schema decoding, error translation, and return projection.
A common writer would need callbacks or branching for one or two outputs, receipt construction, directory custody, chmod sequencing, and capability-specific recovery.
Those callbacks would move security-relevant control flow away from its call site and create combinations that no current caller needs.
Generalising across Photon would reverse or widen the existing package boundary and admit absolute-path and create-only-secret custody concerns into infrastructure.
preserveBoundary: Keep each authority reader, task Schema, size bound, path-conflict rule, result shape, and error mapping at its current capability owner.
Keep Photon authority and create-only binding custody package-local.
Do not add a utils, common, or shared module, a new package, or a new public export.
Do not change current provider, receipt, runbook, authority, or critical-journey behavior.
resumeTrigger: Resume only when at least two current infrastructure callers need the same raw-byte-to-bounded-result operation with identical path policy, size bound, Ajv options, task-policy interface, output count, return shape, and error contract, and a directly tested candidate demonstrably reduces total security-policy surfaces without callbacks or a new public export.
limitations: This is a static repository inspection of the seven infrastructure authority-envelope consumers at the target-derived working tree.
Supporting tests cover task policies and result contracts unevenly; they do not constitute one cross-caller file-boundary property.
Deferral retains visible repetition and requires future hardening to be applied deliberately at each owner.
nonClaims: No shared capability was implemented or proved unsafe in every future design.
No current caller was shown to accept an invalid authority artifact.
No provider, credential, state, deployment, messaging, billing, Preview, Production, or external system was read or mutated.
This decision grants no authority and does not add FINDING-005 to the accepted implementation crosswalk.
